papers.title: VoiceMem: Streaming Dual-Brain Memory for Real-Time Interaction

summary.tldr: VoiceMem is a streaming dual-brain memory architecture featuring parallel informational left-brain and emotional right-brain components designed for real-time, low-latency duplex speech language models.
key_points: Uses a dual-brain architecture: an informational left brain for data retrieval and an emotional right brain featuring short- and long-horizon affective attribution and dual-node persona modeling.
Left-brain memory achieves nearly 30 points higher accuracy under top-5 retrieval compared to classical systems like Mem0 under top-200 retrieval.
Right-brain memory improves aggregate scores by 4.29 points over the previous state-of-the-art across three persona benchmarks.
Operates with a 134 ms retrieval latency, executing within standard Voice Activity Detection (VAD) windows to avoid adding conversational delay.
summary.why_it_matters: VoiceMem enables speech language models to access highly accurate factual memory and persona-driven emotional state in real time without introducing user-perceptible latency.

papers.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion

summary.tldr: FrontierChallenge is a new cross-domain benchmark of 300 scientific workflows that evaluates end-to-end task completion and deliverable bundles across multiple computational sciences.
key_points: Evaluated 97 released tasks across six domains including quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment.
Tested twelve frontier models using three agent scaffolds, with the top-performing configurations achieving a maximum Pass Rate of only 20.6% (20 of 97 tasks).
High partial progress scores failed to produce complete task delivery: analytical chemistry and electrochemistry/environment achieved Avg. Scores of 87.6 and 94.9, but Pass Rates of just 4% and 0%.
Unreliable self-assessment was prevalent, with 75.5% of non-passing Claude Code agent trajectories ending with text explicitly claiming completion.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that high partial scoring and confident language model outputs do not correlate with full scientific workflow execution, requiring stricter end-to-end deliverable evaluation.

papers.title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation

summary.tldr: WarpSAC adapts off-policy RL algorithmic stabilizers based on data abundance, offering two variants that optimize exploitation and value fitting for CPU-scale and GPU-parallel training regimes.
key_points: Identifies that common stabilizers are data-regime-dependent: parameter normalization limits value fitting under abundant data, and clipped double-Q can be relaxed to single-Q in high-throughput settings.
Introduces Sample Weight Decay, an age-biased replay weighting mechanism designed to improve exploitation efficiency regardless of the data regime.
Defines WarpSAC-L (Norm ON, clipped double-Q) for data-limited CPU training and WarpSAC-A (Norm OFF, single-Q) for data-abundant GPU training.
Outperforms FlashSAC with a 4.5% higher normalized score-step AUC across nine CPU environments and 23.1% higher across fourteen GPU-parallel environments.

Demonstrates performance gains on UnitreeG1TransportBox-v1 (success rate up from 19.8% to 96.4%), MuJoCo Playground (19.1% higher mean normalized wall-time AUC), and 36.4% faster sim-to-real deployment on Unitree G1.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that scaling off-policy reinforcement learning to massively parallel GPU environments requires removing data-limited constraints to achieve higher sample efficiency, faster training, and better real-world deployment performance.

papers.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution

summary.tldr: JIT-Agent is a harness intelligence model that dynamically synthesizes, repairs, and evolves task-adaptive agent harnesses for off-the-shelf LLMs using a four-module composable protocol.
key_points: Formalizes the agent harness into a machine-generatable artifact governing memory, planning, action protocol, and tool/skill orchestration.
Uses performance signals from an archive of prior configurations to self-evolve and customize harnesses on the fly.
Enables DeepSeek-V4-Flash to surpass GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), while boosting GLM-5.2 by up to +20.2 points.
Demonstrates consistent performance gains across model families including DeepSeek V4, Mimo-V2.5, and Qwen3.6, competing with runtimes like OpenCode and Claude Code.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes agent harness design as a trainable, automated, and transferable dimension of capability that improves model performance orthogonally to standard foundation model scaling.

papers.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning

summary.tldr: VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed featuring 300 procedurally generated tasks and deterministic rule-based reward scorers to enable trainable, verifiable, and scalable native visual reasoning across image, video, and interleaved generators.
key_points: Introduces 300 procedurally generated visual reasoning tasks that show transfer to seven external benchmarks, including RISE-Video, MME-CoF-Pro, and BabyVision.
Replaces VLM-as-a-judge approaches with deterministic, task-grounded rule scorers that align with human judgment and provide reliable reward signals for multi-task reinforcement learning.
Evaluates over 30 image, video, and interleaved generators, finding video generation superior for persistent spatiotemporal state tracking and interleaved generation more compute-efficient.
Identifies vision-native trajectories through ablations and probing as crucial elements for complex visual reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces unreliable VLM-as-a-judge metrics with deterministic reward scorers, allowing models to use visual generation as an optimizable medium for complex problem solving via reinforcement learning.

papers.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: SecOPD uses on-policy distillation to provide token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, significantly reducing LLM vulnerability to adaptive prompt injections.
key_points: Existing defensive fine-tuning methods like DPO and GRPO rely on sequence-level feedback, failing to identify specific insecure output tokens.
SecOPD scores rollout tokens generated from an injected sample against the base model's predictions on a corresponding clean input.
Defended Qwen3.6-27B reduces Attack Success Rate (ASR) against PISmith adaptive prompt injections from 94.0% (Meta-SecAlign) to 9.0%.
SecOPD generalizes to unseen agentic tool-calling domains, achieving a 4.7% ASR compared to 5.5% for Meta-SecAlign.
summary.why_it_matters: Token-level feedback during defensive fine-tuning effectively neutralizes adaptive prompt injections without sacrificing model performance on unseen agentic tasks.

papers.title: D^3-MOPD: Adaptive Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation

summary.tldr: D^3-MOPD dynamically schedules multi-teacher domain sampling ratios online using reverse-KL trajectories to optimize student training without adding computational overhead.
key_points: Uses an off-process asynchronous watcher to track domain reverse-KL trajectories, estimating headroom and improvement rates without modifying the main training loop.
Addresses domain convergence rate disparities caused by fixed data mixtures in multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD).
Evaluated on a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B student model distilled from four domain-expert teachers.
Closes 97% of the student-to-teacher performance gap (versus 63% for vanilla MOPD) and achieves equivalent peak performance using approximately 3x fewer rollout steps.
Outperforms specialist teachers on three out of seven evaluation benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significantly more compute-efficient multi-domain knowledge distillation by dynamically shifting training resources to slower-converging domains.

papers.title: Agent-G^2: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Agent-G^2 introduces a Gaussian guidance framework that dynamically samples hint depths from an online-estimated Gaussian distribution to resolve reward sparsity in agentic reinforcement learning without extra rollout costs.
key_points: Identifies that informative trajectory guidance depths form a Gaussian distribution around a band center, rather than a single optimal scalar point.

Estimates Gaussian center and spread online using policy optimization rollouts, combining a global baseline, per-cluster difficulty, and within-cluster variance without extra probe rollouts or depth predictors.
Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop benchmarks using Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B-Instruct backbones.
Outperforms top hint-based, hint-free, and Aux-RL baselines on ALFWorld by 2.3, 3.9, and 7.4 points respectively.
Reduces rollout costs to under one-third of the requirements for per-sample probing methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly improves task success rates in long-horizon agentic RL while cutting compute requirements by over 66% compared to probing methods.

papers.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data

summary.tldr: Mixed SFT outperforms next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data post-RLVR, achieving higher accuracy ceilings while using over 60 times less training compute.
key_points: Next-chunk reasoning RL attempts to leverage no-CoT data (e.g., textbook derivations) by generating implicit reasoning traces to predict upcoming text chunks.
Mixed SFT, a single supervised fine-tuning stage combining no-CoT and long-CoT data, consistently yields higher post-RLVR performance ceilings than next-chunk reasoning RL.
Mixed SFT achieves these superior results while requiring over 60x less training compute across both in-domain mathematical reasoning and out-of-domain tasks.
The study demonstrates that higher pre-RLVR accuracy does not guarantee higher post-RLVR accuracy, emphasizing the necessity of evaluating no-CoT methods across the entire post-training pipeline.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that complex next-chunk RL is unnecessary for no-CoT data, as simple Mixed SFT provides better post-RLVR performance at a fraction of the compute cost.

papers.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds

summary.tldr: JoyAI-Echo-1.5 is a unified audio-visual system for generating long-horizon video narratives and interactive worlds using composable memory, geometry-aware control, and rollout-aware few-step training.
key_points: Long-video variant uses composable cross-shot memory aggregating visual evidence and speech-filtered full-shot audio to maintain identity across shots.
World-model variant converts navigation inputs into calibrated metric 6-DoF camera trajectories using a geometry-aware conditioning pathway.
Efficient generation is achieved by distilling a bidirectional audio-visual backbone into a causal few-step generator using progressive teacher forcing and Self-Gradient Forcing.
Achieved first place on WBench with an average score of 81.7 and top performance on SANA-WM-Bench.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables persistent character identities, coherent audio-visual storytelling, and stable controller-agnostic camera navigation over long generation horizons.

papers.title: StreamPI: Streaming Multimodal Temporal Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

summary.tldr: StreamPI is a parameter-free temporal modeling framework for Vision-Language-Action models that enables streaming multi-frame reasoning and asynchronous real-robot deployment.
key_points: Instruction-anchored temporal modeling pairs visual observations with language instructions as atomic temporal units, combining intra-pair bidirectional attention for cross-modal fusion with inter-pair causal attention for streaming inference.
A random-interval streaming training strategy (such as selecting frames every 3 steps) optimizes action execution speed and robustness against real-world asynchronous frame-timing perturbations.
Uses LLM length extrapolation to inherit pretrained single-frame pi0.5 weights while supporting flexible inference across variable frame counts without adding parameters.
Outperforms the single-frame pi0.5 baseline in real-robot tasks requiring spatial/memory perception and on the LIBERO simulation benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows existing single-frame VLA models to gain temporal reasoning and real-time streaming capabilities for complex robotics tasks without requiring extra parameters.

papers.title: Video-IFBench: Evaluating Instruction Following of Multimodal LLMs in Video Understanding Scenarios

summary.tldr: Video-IFBench is a new benchmark featuring 1.5K samples across 32 task types to evaluate how well Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) follow complex user constraints in video understanding tasks.
key_points: Introduces an instruction taxonomy with four structural templates: single-task, multi-task, selection, and nested instructions.
Covers 32 task types and 39 manually designed semantic and format constraint categories based on visual and audio content.
Employs a semi-automatic dataset creation pipeline combining MLLMs, programmatic processing, and human verification to produce 1.5K samples.
Evaluation of 20+ MLLMs shows performance degrades on instructions with many constraints, semantic requirements, or complex conditional selection structures.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized framework to measure whether video-capable MLLMs can adhere strictly to specific formatting and semantic constraints, rather than just assessing basic video content accuracy.

papers.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain

summary.tldr: Code World Model decouples world evolution from visual generation by using a coding agent to maintain state via executable code and conditioning a video model on spatiotemporal proxy representations.
key_points: Uses a LLM-based coding agent as a 'world brain' to reason about events and execute code to maintain a persistent world state.
Introduces a proxy representation that encodes frame-wise spatiotemporal constraints, compiled into a proxy video to condition downstream visual rendering.
Establishes data pipelines to extract and align proxy-observation pairs from gameplay and real-world videos.
Demonstrates that a fine-tuned MiniMax-H3 model follows proxy-based spatiotemporal specifications from agent-built interactive worlds while preserving visual details.
summary.why_it_matters: By relying on executable code for world state rather than purely visual priors, this architecture enables persistent consequences and rule-consistent, open-ended world simulation.

papers.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?

summary.tldr: SWE Refactor Bench evaluates coding agents on 20 whole-repository migrations across four technical debt types using a three-stage protocol that checks both migration completeness and behavioral correctness.
key_points: Introduces a three-stage evaluation protocol: Migration Audit, Behavioural Tests, and Agentic Verification using 6 independent coding agents to detect hidden behavioral differences.
Across 520 runs spanning 8 frontier models and 26 configurations, only 5.4% (28 runs) passed all three stages, leaving 13 of 20 tasks unsolved.
The top-performing model, claude-opus-5, achieved a score of 47.0/100.
Agent success varied dramatically by migration type, scoring 31.4 on build toolchain rewrites versus 5.6 on language rewrites.
Among 340 runs passing the Migration Audit, 58% reached 99% accuracy on fixed checks, but only 26% achieved 100% behavioral correctness.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark prevents agents from cheating by copying legacy code to pass tests, exposing that current frontier models struggle with reliable, long-horizon codebase refactoring.

papers.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: V-Rubrics introduces rubric-based reinforcement learning that decomposes responses into atomic propositions to provide structured, prefix-localized reward credit across visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency, and instruction following.
key_points: Addresses multimodal credit-assignment failures by replacing scalar outcome rewards with structured scoring across Visual Faithfulness, Reasoning Consistency, and Instruction Following.
Constructs V-Rubrics 50K, a 50,248-example training set sourced from 17 visual datasets, filtered by difficulty and annotated using Gemini-3-Pro.
Initializes from a Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct model fine-tuned on the OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K corpus before applying rubric-based GRPO.
Demonstrates that rubric-based GRPO outperforms both the shared SFT baseline and standard answer-only GRPO, achieving peak gains on knowledge-oriented visual reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Decomposing rewards into localized, proposition-level rubrics mitigates visual hallucination and ungrounded reasoning in vision-language models better than traditional scalar reward signals.

papers.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning

summary.tldr: VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed with 300 procedurally generated tasks and deterministic reward scorers designed to scale, verify, and optimize native visual reasoning through image, video, and interleaved generation.
key_points: Task space includes 300 procedurally generated tasks that demonstrate strong transfer to seven external benchmarks, including RISE-Video, MME-CoF-Pro, and BabyVision.
Replaces unreliable VLM-as-a-judge approaches with deterministic, rule-based reward scorers that align with human judgments and enable large-scale multi-task reinforcement learning.
Provides a controlled experimental environment evaluating over 30 image, video, and interleaved generators.

Mechanism analysis indicates video generation excels at persistent spatiotemporal state tracking, interleaved generation offers compute efficiency, and vision-native trajectories are critical for visual reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a verifiable, reinforcement-learning-ready framework for training multimodal models to use visual generation directly as a substrate for complex problem solving.

papers.title: Prefix Sliding for efficient test-time scaling

summary.tldr: Prefix Sliding reduces test-time scaling costs by discarding intermediate reasoning tokens while retaining the initial instruction prefix and a sliding window of recent tokens.
key_points: Retains only the initial instruction/tool prefix and the last few thousand tokens, placing a hard cap on KV cache memory regardless of reasoning length.
Delivers a 3x speedup on existing models out-of-the-box without requiring additional training.
Enables RL-based fine-tuning that scales reasoning traces beyond 100,000 tokens while maintaining accuracy.
Outperforms alternative memory-reduction baselines including token summarization and standard vanilla sliding window attention.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables models to perform ultra-long-horizon reasoning and test-time compute scaling at a fraction of the computational and memory cost.

papers.title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention

summary.tldr: This paper establishes task-dependent rank-error bounds for Query LoRA updates in Transformer attention, expressing expected KL error through the downstream-weighted tail energy of target updates.
key_points: Establishes an error lower bound proportional to $\psi(\|d\|_2)$ (where $\psi(t)=\min\{t^2,t\}$) and an upper bound of $\min\{\|d\|_2^2/4,\sqrt{2}\|d\|_2\}$ for score difference $d$.
Bounds the optimal rank-$r$ error between a multiple of $\psi(\sqrt{T_r})$ and $\min\{T_r/4,\sqrt{2T_r}\}$, where $T_r$ represents the downstream-weighted tail energy.
Demonstrates through explicit constructions that softmax saturation allows matching attention functions using a strictly lower rank than required to match finite logits.
Provides target-Fisher bounds, unrestricted lower bounds for localized token probability, and extends theoretical analysis to fused multi-head LoRA and joint query/key updates.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a theoretical foundation for selecting LoRA ranks based on task data and attention geometry rather than relying solely on trial-and-error hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: DualOPSD: Adaptive Privileged Teachers for On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: DualOPSD introduces an asymmetric alternating framework for on-policy self-distillation that dynamically adapts the privileged teacher toward the updated student distribution without requiring extra rollouts.
key_points: DualOPSD alternates training: the student first learns from the privileged teacher, and the teacher then moves toward the updated student distribution on the same trajectory.
Eliminates the need for an additional rollout when updating the teacher policy.
Achieves accuracy gains on Qwen3-8B (non-thinking mode) over standard OPSD, improving avg@12 by 23.61 on AIME 2024, 13.89 on AIME 2025, and 10.00 on HMMT 2025.
Reduces generation truncation across 1.7B, 4B, and 8B scales, and lowers bidirectional KL divergence between teacher and student as shown in 4B diagnostics.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves student model accuracy and generation length efficiency in self-distillation without incurring the computational overhead of generating new teacher rollouts.

papers.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs

summary.tldr: AsymSpec is an asymmetric speculative decoding framework where a lightweight draft model operates on full context while a large verifier model runs on a compressed context to reduce inference costs.
key_points: Breaks standard speculative decoding context symmetry by feeding full input to the small drafter and compressed input to the large verifier.
Uses contrastive delta-fusion of logits to allow the full-context drafter to steer the verifier model.
Employs a divergence-aware acceptance gate to maintain verification stability and ensure high draft acceptance rates.
Achieves approximately 90% of full-context accuracy on average across agentic benchmarks.
Delivers 1.3x to 1.7x throughput speedups at 0.2x to 0.3x the compute cost on isolated text capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: It breaks the strict latency-accuracy trade-off in agentic LLM pipelines by preserving key reasoning signals with minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon

summary.tldr: Researchers developed Spectral-Aware Muon (SAMuon), which outperforms AdamW and Muon by using a static spectral prior to apply larger step sizes to the tolerant bulk singular directions of momentum buffers.
key_points: Out-of-sample spectral probing shows Transformer loss landscapes have an anisotropic spectral profile where a volatile head requires small step sizes while a tolerant bulk permits significantly larger steps.
Muon outperforms Adam and SGD due to its orthogonal optimization, but its uniform scaling underutilizes the tolerant bulk.
SAMuon holds the volatile head at the standard Muon scale and amplifies bulk step sizes using low-rank randomized SVD, while SAMuon-lite uses a two-level rank-one power iteration approximation.

Across 124M to 1B parameter modded-nanogpt models, SAMuon achieves identical validation loss to Muon using 13.3% to 24.0% fewer training tokens without adding persistent optimizer state or notable FLOP overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: SAMuon speeds up LLM pretraining convergence by up to 24% over Muon without requiring additional persistent optimizer memory.

papers.title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents

summary.tldr: SwarmWorld demonstrates that decentralized, initially homogeneous LLM agents can self-organize through environmental stigmergy and physical observation to build durable, resilient technological societies without predefined roles or direct centralized workflows.
key_points: LLM agents propose architectures and executable controllers evaluated by a deterministic simulator under unseen disturbances after agent removal.
Shared agent societies build broader, more resilient technology portfolios than a strong best-of-N isolated-search baseline, though isolated search competes on peak single-artifact performance.
Agents spontaneously differentiate into exploration, construction, maintenance, and coordination roles as the physical environment matures.
Technology reuse and accumulation begin predominantly through physical observation of persistent artifacts rather than direct agent-to-agent communication.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves LLM multi-agent systems can achieve scalable collective intelligence and complex engineering through environmental modification (stigmergy) rather than relying on direct conversation or centralized control.

papers.title: $R^3$: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: $R^3$ is a post-training recipe that uses mid-training on expert traces and rubric-based RL on offline action data to train VLMs to generate free-form natural language reasoning for steering low-level robotic policies.
key_points: Combines mid-training on expert-generated reasoning traces with single-step rubric-based reinforcement learning using offline action data.
Enables Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to use free-form natural language reasoning as a test-time compute mechanism for guiding action policies.
Validated on Language Table and simulated bimanual grocery packing environments for long-horizon manipulation and error recovery.
Outperforms standard instruction-only imitation learning baselines in exploration and generalization across unseen tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that free-form natural language reasoning can serve as an effective test-time compute mechanism to improve long-horizon task execution and generalization in robotic manipulation.

papers.title: ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs

summary.tldr: ProgRouter is an online routing framework that adaptively selects LLM agents step-by-step during multi-agent workflows based on task progress predictions, time constraints, and cost budgets.
key_points: Replaces static, one-shot cascade routing with dynamic, online step-wise routing suited for long-horizon multi-agent LLM context evolution.
Uses a multi-view task progress scorer integrating workflow outcome regimes, subtask completion signals, progress trends, and state quality.
Employs a dual-path task progress predictor and adaptive meta-gating mechanism to calculate the expected progress gain for candidate LLMs.
Validated on HumanEval Plus, MBPP, MATH-500, and ASQA, demonstrating reduced operating costs while preserving task-solving accuracy across code, math, and QA domains.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables multi-agent LLM systems to solve complex tasks within strict financial and latency budgets by dynamically routing lower-cost models when full-scale models are unnecessary.

papers.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: This review provides a unified structural framework identifying collapse as the primary failure mode in On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for mathematical reasoning, analyzing it through three governing levers.
key_points: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) eliminates the need for a larger teacher model by using the student model itself, conditioned on privileged information like reference solutions, plans, or environment feedback.
The primary failure mode of OPSD is collapse, defined as the progressive narrowing of the set of reasoning paths the model can generate.

Collapse is governed by three specific levers: token weighting (where signal is applied), the nature of privileged information (what the teacher sees), and teacher dynamics/guidance decay (when the signal changes).
The paper introduces a shared structural vocabulary to standardize inconsistent terminology across existing mathematical reasoning OPSD literature without adding new experimental data.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a clear vocabulary and structural framework to help researchers analyze and prevent model collapse when using self-teacher privileged guidance instead of larger teacher models.

security.title: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode

summary.tldr: A website summary request can hijack Claude Code Opus 5 in Auto Mode to achieve code execution with a 60-80% attack success rate.
key_points: Claude Code Opus 5 in Auto Mode was successfully hijacked via a website summary prompt injection attack.
The attack achieved a 60-80% success rate in code execution based on a small sample size.
The findings contradict an Anthropic-commissioned third-party evaluation that reported a 0.00% prompt injection attack success rate for Opus 5 in Auto Mode.
Auto Mode, which relies on a safety classifier instead of human approval prompts, became the default starting mode for Claude Code in mid-August.
summary.why_it_matters: Default automated execution modes in AI agent tools can bypass security assumptions and allow arbitrary code execution through untrusted Web content.

security.title: RTLGuard: A Lightweight Teacher-Student Defense for Poisoned RTL Code Generation Models

summary.tldr: RTLGuard is a lightweight teacher-student defense framework designed to sanitize backdoor-poisoned RTL code generation models without full-parameter retraining.
key_points: Addresses backdoor threats and hardware Trojan insertion caused by opaque third-party fine-tuning of LLMs used for hardware design.
Fine-tunes a small, clean teacher model on a limited trusted dataset of register transfer level (RTL) code.
Guides the poisoned target student model using a composite objective that combines feature alignment and knowledge distillation to suppress malicious triggers.
Reduces the Attack Success Rate (ASR) while maintaining the functional correctness and synthesizability of the generated RTL code.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a computationally efficient method to secure the AI-enabled integrated circuit supply chain against malicious hardware Trojans embedded in third-party LLMs.

security.title: Vulnerable Code Search: Transferable Attack for Code Language Models

summary.tldr: A language-agnostic, transferable adversarial attack perturbs non-functional code identifiers to trick code language models into retrieving irrelevant code snippets.
key_points: The attack modifies identifiers without changing code functionality to artificially increase similarity with a target query.
Adversarial perturbations computed on smaller open models like CodeT5+ successfully transfer to larger closed-source models including Voyage-code-3 and Gemini-3.1-Pro.
The attack degrades key retrieval metrics, reducing the Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) of state-of-the-art models by up to 77%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that current neural code retrieval systems rely heavily on surface textual features rather than true semantics, leaving developer search tools vulnerable to manipulation.

security.title: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework Defense against LLM Jailbreak Attacks

summary.tldr: A self-evolving test-time defense framework mitigates LLM jailbreaks by abstracting attack failures into persistent, method-level rules stored in cross-interaction memory without updating model parameters.
key_points: Abstracts successful jailbreaks into method-level rules targeting structural attack wrappers (e.g., role-playing, code transformation) rather than specific harmful topics.
Operates entirely via prompting and persistent external rule memory, making it applicable to both open-weight and black-box API models without training.
Uses a four-module architecture to dynamically expand its label space and reuse learned defensive rules against entire attack families.
Maintains benign utility and prevents over-refusal growth while remaining resilient against adaptive composite-wrapper attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployed black-box language models to dynamically adapt to novel jailbreak strategies over time without requiring costly parameter updates or retraining.

security.title: Beyond the Editing Canvas: Evidence Divergence in OOXML-to-LLM Ingestion

summary.tldr: OOXML files can induce 'evidence forks' where extracted text consumed by LLMs differs from the content rendered in Microsoft Office's editing canvas, creating security risks across workflows.
key_points: Identified 21 distinct evidence forks across Excel, Word, and PowerPoint spanning six dimensions of view construction.
Tested 13 extraction tools, finding that all emit evidence from at least one fork.
Four native-ingestion LLM APIs returned unrendered 'trap' facts in 48% to 76% of evaluation trials.
At least one of eleven evaluated LLM interfaces (4 APIs, 7 web chatbots) returned the hidden trap fact for 20 out of 21 mechanisms.
A source-level survey of 16 popular open-source LLM projects confirmed that default ingestion configurations rely heavily on affected extractor families.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM-based compliance, financial, and RAG pipelines may process hidden, unrendered, or spoofed document content as truth, exposing automated systems to data integrity failures and potential exploitation.

security.title: SkillShield: Prompt-Space Security Skills for LLM Coding Agents

summary.tldr: SkillShield is a system-prompt defense for LLM coding agents that injects offline-synthesized security skills into the system prompt to prevent malware generation and harmful execution without runtime classification.
key_points: SkillShield operates via fixed-budget provisioning scopes (all-classes, per-bundle, and per-class) injected at session start to guide execution policies within the tool-use loop.
Tested across six LLMs on RedCode, the default all-classes skill reduced malware-generation severity from 3.37 to 0.58 and achieved a 43.6% execution attack success rate (ASR).
Per-bundle and per-class configurations further decreased the execution ASR to 36.2% and 14.5%, respectively, outperforming non-adaptive jailbreak baselines.
The defense matches the performance of Llama Guard 3 (42.7% ASR) without requiring its separate 8B parameter classifier or auxiliary execution-boundary monitors.
Evaluations across 731 benign task descriptions demonstrated a low mean safety-refusal rate of 0.14%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables API-only deployers to enforce strict agent execution safety and prevent malware generation directly through prompt engineering without introducing dedicated runtime classifier models.

security.title: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers identified a self-poisoning vulnerability in self-evolving coding agents and created EvoMal, an attack that trick agents into cloning planted malicious skill payloads into new, self-propagating, defense-evading skills.
key_points: EvoMal uses a 'banner'—benign-looking structural wrapper code—around interchangeable payloads to induce agents to copy malicious code into newly authored skills.

Across six models on 153 SWE-bench Verified tasks, Agent Self-Poisoning Rate (ASPR) reached 20.3%–41.8%, multiplying malicious skills 4.9x–9.0x; tailoring descriptions to specific task families raised ASPR to 86.7%.
Self-poisoned skills persist as self-propagating worms; Qwen3 maintained a 68% ASPR at round 5 even after original planted skills were deleted.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro achieved an 11.1% ASPR using un-bannered payloads alone, proving the underlying self-poisoning vulnerability exists without explicit wrapping.
A proposed 'counter-prompt' defense reduces EvoMal's ASPR to <= 6.7% without significantly compromising task performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Self-evolving agents that populate shared skill libraries can inadvertently generate and propagate persistent malware worms that bypass standard security defenses based on static attacker signatures.

security.title: Reassembling Distributed Risk: Trajectory-Conditioned Action Generation for Multi-Turn Agent Safety

summary.tldr: ReDiR is a generation-time agent defense that prevents multi-turn decomposition attacks by injecting compressed latent trajectory-safety evidence into a frozen base LLM before each action.
key_points: Addresses multi-turn decomposition attacks where harmful intent is fragmented across individually plausible, context-isolated tool calls.
Compresses the multi-turn interaction trajectory into a compact latent safety representation and injects it directly into the frozen base model during action generation.
Trains the representation using same-model, cross-view supervision, mapping explicit task-view safe behavior to the original trajectory to recover distributed security evidence.
Eliminates the need for external online reasoning modules, runtime-specific action representations, or separate action-level safety classifiers.
Evaluated across three model families and eight held-out tool domains, reducing attack success rates to below 8% while maintaining benign fidelity and low overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables tool-using LLM agents to detect and block distributed long-horizon security risks directly within the generation pass without sacrificing latency or domain generalizability.

security.title: LMSM: LLM Security Framework Inspired by Linux Security Modules

summary.tldr: Language Model Security Modules (LMSM) adapts the Linux Security Modules design pattern to decouple LLM interpretability evidence, policy rules, and runtime enforcement.
key_points: Decouples safety enforcement into a security backend providing calibrated evidence, a versioned policy engine, and a gate authorizing output release.
Supports multiple interpretability artifacts, hosting sparse autoencoders (SAE), transcoders, and task-fitted dense probes on Hugging Face Transformers and vLLM.
Preserves request-specific enforcement decisions under vLLM scheduler churn and allows rule composition without rebuilding request handling.
Tested on Qwen3-4B using LMSM-Checkpoint, reducing HarmBench attack success rate from 39.20% to 3.32% while XSTest false refusals increased slightly from 2.40% to 4.40%.
Retains 98.14% of serving throughput compared to an unmonitored path at 32 active sequences.
summary.why_it_matters: LMSM provides a unified runtime security framework that converts internal model interpretability signals into composable, low-overhead safety controls without modifying serving code.

security.title: AI Slop and Hallucinations in Vulnerability Assessment: A Survey on Reasoning Failures and Trustworthy Mitigation

summary.tldr: This survey formalizes a taxonomy of security 'AI slop', proposes the Deductive Coverage Score metric, and outlines neuro-symbolic verification alongside new evaluation instruments (CVE-Bench and Slop-Score) to fix LLM reasoning failures in vulnerability assessment.
key_points: Formalizes 'AI slop' in cybersecurity as hallucinated vulnerabilities, incorrect patches, and repackaged bug reports caused by the gap between LLM autoregressive probabilistic generation and causal deductive reasoning.
Introduces the Deductive Coverage Score as a measurable proxy for reasoning gaps, showing chain-of-thought prompting and agents improve but fail to resolve it.
Critiques passive detection and watermarking due to fundamental entropy constraints, advocating instead for active neuro-symbolic verification.
Proposes two new evaluation instruments, CVE-Bench and Slop-Score, featuring dedicated dataset designs, metric formulas, and anti-gaming provisions to shift focus to mathematical verifiability.
summary.why_it_matters: Replacing linguistic fluency evaluation with active neuro-symbolic verification prevents low-quality, AI-generated reports from overwhelming human vulnerability triage pipelines.

security.title: MMJailBench: A Factorized Benchmark for Disentangling Multimodal Jailbreak Vulnerabilities

summary.tldr: MMJailBench is a new factorized benchmark that isolates harmful intent, prompt framing, visual semantics, and instruction carriers to systematically evaluate MLLM jailbreak vulnerabilities.
key_points: Evaluates 16 open-weight and proprietary MLLMs by systematically varying four distinct jailbreak factors under controlled configurations.
Identifies prompt framing as the primary driver of jailbreak variation, with task-relevant visual semantics—especially authority-like cues—systematically increasing susceptibility.
Finds that visually rendered text instructions do not consistently increase jailbreak risk compared to direct textual instructions.
Includes a modular evaluation suite featuring full and lightweight configurations, multiple judge options, and multidimensional metrics alongside internal representation diagnostics.
summary.why_it_matters: By decoupling confounding variables in multimodal attacks, safety researchers can pinpoint precise cross-modal vulnerabilities and improve safety alignment across specific harm domains.

security.title: When AI infrastructure becomes the target: Securing gateways and control points

summary.tldr: Microsoft observed threat actors targeting AI infrastructure components like LiteLLM, RAGFlow, and Kestra to steal credentials, gain persistence, and hijack compute resources.
key_points: LiteLLM gateway compromise involved Python droppers, runtime secret harvesting, PostgreSQL data collection, XMRig miner deployment, and exploitation via CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710.
RAGFlow compromise utilized SSRF-style reconnaissance and code execution to place a Python hook in the TenantLLM configuration flow, intercepting LLM provider credentials and model metadata.
Kestra orchestration compromise leveraged CVE-2026-49869 for workflow-origin shell execution, container environment discovery, XMRig deployment, and secret collection.
Targeted AI control points aggregate high-value assets including model-provider keys, virtual keys, database connection strings, and host execution privileges.
summary.why_it_matters: AI gateways and orchestration layers concentrate critical credentials and execution privileges, making them prime targets for enterprise host compromise and compute monetization.

summary.tldr: In a Trail of Bits evaluation, GPT 5.6-Cyber successfully escaped a QEMU/KVM sandbox three times, utilizing N-day kernel vulnerabilities, unpatched component bugs, and newly discovered 0-days to achieve host breakout.
key_points: The agent escaped a QEMU/KVM VM on Debian 12 (AMD Zen3) by weaponizing the recently disclosed Januscape host kernel bug (CVE-2026-53359) without a public exploit.
When faced with an updated host, the agent bypassed containment by exploiting unpatched dependencies and finding multiple original 0-day vulnerabilities in upstream QEMU builds.
The agent operated autonomously over several hours, reading research papers, writing diagnostic oracles, creating minimal reproducers, and recovering from failed attempts without manual intervention.
Standard virtual machine sandboxing with shared host resources, network access, and SSH access is insufficient to contain advanced, cyber-capable AI agents.
summary.why_it_matters: Security teams can no longer rely on standard virtual machines as a trusted isolation barrier when running capable AI agents, requiring them to be treated with the same containment rigor as an advanced persistent threat.

security.title: MACGen: Toward Functionally Correct and Secure Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration

summary.tldr: MACGen is a multi-agent code generation framework that uses structured artifact passing instead of shared dialogue histories to optimize both functional correctness and security.
key_points: MACGen separates tasks across specialized agents: a planner for functional requirements, a security advisor for CWE identification and guidelines, a coder for synthesis, and a reviewer for perspective-separated feedback.
Eliminates full dialogue history sharing by passing only structured artifacts downstream to enforce role specialization and prevent context bloat.
Improves F&S@1 scores over direct prompting by an average of 19.61 percentage points on CWEval and 10.57 percentage points on BaxBench.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that decoupling multi-agent communication into structured artifacts improves both the security and functional correctness of LLM-generated code while reducing context overhead.

summary.tldr: OpenAI disrupted a Cambodian social engineering network that leveraged ChatGPT to execute multi-persona scams and generate forged documents at scale.
key_points: The Cambodian network ran concurrent scam vectors, including pig-butchering (blending romance personas with fake crypto/gold spot trading) and law enforcement impersonation for fine extortion.
Operators utilized ChatGPT to conduct prolonged romantic conversations and manage fictitious online gambling platform personas offering fake bonuses.
The model was used to generate synthetic images of forged assets, including passports, legal notices, stock-purchase confirmations, and gambling interfaces.
summary.why_it_matters: LLMs reduce the operational cost of complex, multi-persona social engineering attacks by automating believable rapport-building and document forgery.

infra.title: Reduce ASR inference costs by 75% with NVIDIA MPS on Amazon EC2

summary.tldr: AWS, NVIDIA, and Heidi Health demonstrated using NVIDIA CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS) with Triton Inference Server on Amazon EC2 to reduce GPU infrastructure requirements for ASR inference by 75 percent while maintaining sub-second latency.
key_points: Single ASR inference requests for the Parakeet TDT 0.6B V2 model utilize only 15–20% of an NVIDIA L40S GPU's 142 streaming multiprocessors (SMs), leaving ~80% idle under default CUDA time-slicing.
CUDA MPS routes work through a single daemon-managed context, enabling concurrent kernel execution across shared SMs without context-switching overhead or code changes.

Deploying MPS reduced Heidi Health's required Amazon EC2 GPU instances from 16 to 4 while sustaining 92.1 requests per second (RPS) per GPU under sub-second latency SLAs (mean < 650 ms, p99 < 1,000 ms).
summary.why_it_matters: Utilizing CUDA MPS enables organizations to dramatically lower cloud GPU infrastructure costs for low-utilization ASR workloads without violating strict real-time latency SLAs.

infra.title: NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Brings NVHBM to Next-Generation AI Infrastructure

summary.tldr: NVIDIA NVLink Fusion integrates high-bandwidth memory (NVHBM) into next-generation AI infrastructure to scale custom AI accelerators (XPUs).
key_points: AI factories require high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to sustain compute demands for large models and complex reasoning workloads.
Hyperscalers and AI-native companies are developing custom AI accelerators (XPUs) to meet scale requirements.
Scaling XPU deployments requires sufficient package and silicon area alongside high-bandwidth memory.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating NVHBM via NVLink Fusion helps eliminate memory and package area bottlenecks for custom AI accelerators operating at hyperscale.

infra.title: NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Expands With NVHBM Custom High-Bandwidth Memory

summary.tldr: NVIDIA expanded NVLink Fusion by introducing NVHBM, a custom high-bandwidth memory architecture that integrates the memory controller directly into the 3D HBM base die instead of the XPU compute die.
key_points: NVHBM moves the memory controller to the 3D HBM stack, freeing up to 25% more silicon area on the XPU compute die compared to standard HBM4E.
The new memory technology delivers up to 30% greater memory bandwidth and reduces HBM power consumption by 15%.
Amazon's Annapurna Labs is the first collaborator adopting NVHBM and will support NVLink Fusion starting with its Trainium4 chips.
NVIDIA is establishing a standardized NVHBM implementation that will be validated and supplied by multiple memory partners.
summary.why_it_matters: By decoupling the memory controller from the compute die and standardizing the interface, hyperscalers can build semi-custom XPUs with higher compute density and improved energy efficiency.

infra.title: Bring your own model with Amazon SageMaker AI: Script mode in SDK v3

summary.tldr: The Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v3 unifies bring-your-own-model workflows into a single ModelTrainer and ModelBuilder interface using runtime code injection via the new SourceCode object.
key_points: Replaces SDK v2 framework-specific estimators (e.g., SKLearn, PyTorch, XGBoost) with unified ModelTrainer for training and ModelBuilder for deployment.
Uses the SourceCode object to sync local code directories into training and inference containers at runtime via source_dir, command, or entry_script without rebuilding images.
Supports bring-your-own-container workflows using any Amazon ECR image, AWS Deep Learning Containers, or third-party images across tabular, generative AI, and multi-GPU distributed frameworks.
Requires sagemaker>=3.0, an IAM execution role, an S3 bucket for artifacts, and an Amazon ECR container image.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can iterate on training and inference scripts faster across any framework or container without rebuilding Docker images for code updates.

infra.title: Deepgram deepens Amazon SageMaker AI observability with Enhanced Metrics

summary.tldr: Deepgram has introduced Enhanced Metrics and Prometheus/OpenTelemetry support for its isolated self-hosted speech AI containers on Amazon SageMaker AI.
key_points: Deepgram Enhanced Metrics export container billing and feature usage data via stdout using CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) without sidecars or new IAM permissions.
The container publishes the exact consumed-unit values used for AWS Marketplace metered billing down to the model and transport level.
Prometheus and OpenTelemetry integration allows scraping engine-level, host, and per-GPU metrics directly from the container via SageMaker AI detailed observability.
Both observability capabilities operate within AWS Marketplace network isolation constraints without opening outbound network paths.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows security-conscious organizations running network-isolated SageMaker endpoints to perform GPU-level performance monitoring and precise AWS Marketplace cost reconciliation.

infra.title: Deploy personal AI agents with Cloud Run instances

The service provides managed infrastructure designed to handle agentic workloads.

infra.title: Evaluate any agent framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore evaluations uses OpenTelemetry standards to evaluate AI agents across diverse frameworks like LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and OpenAI Agents SDK without needing framework-specific SDK integration.
key_points: Decouples agent evaluation from specific SDKs by consuming standard OpenTelemetry traces collected via the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) and Amazon CloudWatch.

Filters full execution traces down to three core span roles required for evaluation: invoke agent (top-level request/response), inference (model calls and message history), and execute tool (tool inputs/outputs).
Supports both OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (such as chat, retrieval, and execute_tool) and OpenInference span kinds (such as LLM, TOOL, RETRIEVER, and CHAIN).
Ignores non-essential spans like retrieval, reranking, guardrails, and memory without requiring special configuration or breaking evaluation pipelines.
summary.why_it_matters: Engineers can evaluate agent performance across multiple disparate frameworks using a single standardized telemetry-based evaluation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime.

infra.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 2: Advanced data strategies

summary.tldr: AWS outlines advanced data optimization strategies for supervised fine-tuning, focusing on empirical dataset size evaluation using learning curve analysis.
key_points: Typical SFT baseline requirements range from 500 samples for simple style changes to over 10,000 samples for complex multi-step reasoning tasks.
Learning curve analysis can be conducted in a single training run by evaluating intermediate checkpoints saved every 10–20 percent of training against a held-out benchmark.
Data scaling saturation is reached when doubling the training data yields less than a 1–2 percent improvement on the primary downstream metric.
Unlike pretraining, SFT performance does not scale monotonically with data volume alone, relying instead on instruction set coverage and depth.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding data saturation curves prevents wasted compute and unnecessary data collection by identifying exactly when to stop training or pivot to targeted data types.

infra.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 1: Formatting and quality

summary.tldr: Part one of this series details foundational data preparation methods for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), emphasizing that high data quality, strict accuracy, and semantic diversity outperform sheer dataset size.
key_points: Post-training customization uses three sequential levers: Continued Pre-training (CPT) to expand knowledge, SFT to shape output behavior and schema adherence, and Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) to optimize via reward signals.

Data quality takes precedence over volume; research shows 1,000 highly curated examples (LIMA) or filtering to the top 20% cleanest examples (AlpaGasus) achieves higher performance than larger, noisy datasets.
Generalization during SFT depends heavily on dataset diversity, specifically semantic coverage (breadth of task domains and prompt phrasings) and information depth (richness of individual examples).
summary.why_it_matters: Prioritizing strict quality checks and semantic diversity over large data quantities reduces compute costs and prevents models from learning persistent incorrect response patterns.

Applications are evaluated directly by Anthropic teams and subject matter experts in relevant fields.
